newsitem.title: USA: Number of US Q2 dividend increases off 12 pct -S&P.
newsitem.headline: Number of US Q2 dividend increases off 12 pct -S&P.

text.p: The number of U.S. companies increasing their dividends in the second quarter fell 12 percent compared with the number in the second quarter of 1996, Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday.
S&P, a unit of the McGraw-Hill Cos Inc, said 496 companies increased their dividends in the second quarter of 1997, down from from 564 in the year-earlier period.
For the first half of 1997, the number of dividend increases dropped 1.2 percent to 1,140 from 1,154 in the first six months of 1996, S&P said.
Only nine companies cut their dividends in the second quarter, compared with 22 in the year-earlier quarter. The number of dividend omissions fell to 17 from 19.

Joseph Tigue, managing editor of The Outlook, Standard & Poor's weekly investment advisory newsletter, said companies may not feel pressured to boost dividends because of the sharp rise in the stock market has led to sizeable capital gains for shareholders.
Corporate managements may also aiming to conserve cash in anticipation of a slowdown in profits, the primary determinant of dividends, Tigue said.
Standard & Poor's said it now expected dividends on the S&P 500 index to increase five percent this year, down from a earlier forecast of seven percent.
Dividends on the S&P 500 rose eight percent in 1996.
